name: Jãs
body:
Jãs
CR 2

This small, hooded fey has a nearly featureless face like a smooth, white oval, save for glowing white eyes. It has wears finely woven skirts and has insectile wings of gold or coppery gossamer.

XP 600
NG Small fey
Init +5; Senses low-light vision; Perception +8; Aura aura of unease (30 feet, DC 15)

DEFENSE

AC 15, touch 14, flat-footed 12 (+3 Dex, +1 natural, +1 size)
hp 18 (4d6+4)
Fort +2, Ref +7, Will +6; +2 vs. charm and compulsion DR 5/cold iron; Immune sleep; Resist fire 5

OFFENSE

Speed 20 ft., fly 40 ft. (good)
Melee spear +0 (1d6–2/x3)
Ranged radiant dart +6 (2d6 nonlethal or positive energy)
Special Attacks radiant dart
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 7th, concentration +10)

Constant—speak with animals (birds only)
At will—invisibility (self only), mending (cloth only), prestidigitation
3/day—faerie fire, warp terrain (see below)
1/day—divination, minor creation (cloth only), sleep (DC 14)

STATISTICS

Str 6, Dex 16, Con 12, Int 12, Wis 15, Cha 16
Base Atk +2; CMB +0; CMD 13
Feats Alertness, Weapon Finesse
Skills Acrobatics +9, Craft (weaving) +15, Escape Artist +7, Fly +10, Knowledge (nature) +7, Perception +8, Sense Motive +6, Stealth +13, Survival +8; Racial Modifier Craft (weaving) +8
Languages Common, Sylvan

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Aura of Unease (Su)

Creatures hostile to the jãs beginning their turn within 30 feet of it take 1d6 points of nonlethal damage (DC 15 Will half). On a failed save, they take a -2 penalty on attack rolls and skill checks against the jãs. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Radiant Dart (Su)

A jãs can hurl a sliver of light as a ranged touch attack with a range of 60 feet. On a hit, it deals 2d6 nonlethal damage to a living creature or 2d6 positive energy damage to an undead.

Warp Terrain (Sp)

A jãs can create an illusion filling a 10-foot square, causing it to appear as a tangled or nigh-impassable area of difficult terrain (DC 15 Will disbelief) of a kind appropriate to the area the spell is cast, lasting 1 minute.

ECOLOGY

Environment temperate forests
Organization solitary, family (2–5), or band (6–10)
Treasure standard

These small creatures live in communion with the land and with clans and villages that follow ancient rites of mystery cults rather than following more modern religions. It is said that they knitted the first linens of humanity thousands of years ago. The jãs are fairy weavers – so skilled that in a matter of hours, they can weave meters and meters of linen (as fine as a strand of hair) without a single imperfection.

These fey beings materialize in the embers of fireplaces after the sun has set. In exchange for their knitting work, they accept bread, wine, or cakes. Despite the benevolence they display, they have a self-interested nature and can be vindictive (it’s said that they’ll burn the provided linen if the offering displeases them).

They can talk with birds and foresee the future in the woven threads. Occasionally, they might abduct human infants and replace them with their own fey or part-fey children (known as Janines), so that these are nursed and grow up outside the fairy realms, later returning their adopted human children with a fey blessing.
